technical_and_design_decisions: Develop all samples and changes against the existing Spring XD samples repository and module framework, using Gradle as the build system, consistent with the existing codebase.

U1 (Kafka pipeline): implement log aggregation as Spring XD streams using Kafka source/sink modules backed by Spring Integration Kafka adapters; implement the lambda architecture demo by factoring shared processing logic into reusable XD processor modules used by both speed (streaming) and batch paths, and use Kafka's retention/replay capability to demonstrate reliable reprocessing instead of duplicating business logic.

U2 and U7 (Sqoop / JDBC-HDFS): implement data movement as Spring XD batch jobs composed of Spring Batch steps that invoke Apache Sqoop for JDBC-to-HDFS and HDFS-to-JDBC transfers; for U7 provide a simpler JDBC-source to HDFS-sink example using standard XD modules where possible.

U4/U5 (Storm and Spark Streaming comparisons): deliver side-by-side implementations of representative Storm/Spark topologies and their Spring XD stream-definition equivalents, plus a mapping document comparing concepts (spout/bolt vs. source/processor/sink, DStream vs. XD stream).

U6 (Smart Grid demo): port the s1-2014 demo by recreating its ingestion, processing, and visualization flows as XD stream definitions and custom modules in the samples repo, reusing original assets where licensing permits.

U8 (file sink naming): add a new --nameExpression option to the file sink module's option metadata and wire it to the filename-generator-expression attribute of the underlying file outbound channel adapter, with SpEL validation and precedence rules relative to existing name/dir options.

U3 (docs build): switch generated documentation handling in the Gradle build, remove the pushGeneratedDocs task and its configuration, and delete the now-unneeded link rewriting step; verify the docs task produces publishable output without them.

Testing approach: JUnit-based unit tests for module code, plus integration tests using an embedded/local Kafka broker, a Hadoop mini-cluster (or single-node pseudo-distributed Hadoop) for HDFS, and a test database (e.g., H2/MySQL) for JDBC scenarios.
assumptions: A single developer (the estimator) performs all work; estimates are effort in 8-hour workdays, not elapsed time, and exclude any waiting/review turnaround by third parties.

The work targets the existing Spring XD codebase and samples repository (Java 8 era stack); the Spring Framework 6 / Java 17 statement in the specification is contextual and does not require migrating Spring XD to Spring 6.

Required infrastructure (Kafka broker, Hadoop/HDFS test cluster, relational database, CI server, Gradle build environment) is available or can be run locally in containers/embedded form; no procurement or environment provisioning time is included beyond build script setup.
Estimates include design, implementation, unit and integration testing, and documentation, but exclude production deployment, operations, and ongoing maintenance.
The s1-2014 Smart Grid demo assets are available and licensed for reuse/porting.
U8 is scoped to the Spring XD file sink module (option metadata and wiring to the existing filename-generator-expression attribute), not a change to core Spring Integration.
User stories U2 and U7 partially overlap (JDBC to HDFS); U7 is estimated as a lightweight standalone example that may reuse U2 artifacts, so it is smaller.
No major defects, scope changes, or external blockers occur; code review rework is accounted for as a dedicated activity.
